item.title: Ericsson to lay off one in ten workers in Sweden
item.description: The Swedish telecommunications giant Ericsson has announced plans to lay off one out of every ten workers in Sweden, a total of 1,600 employees, as it seeks to bolster its competitiveness.

item.title: Social Democrats back plan to strip citizenship for 'harming Sweden's interests'
item.description: The Social Democrats will now back a government proposal to allow Swedish citizenship to be stripped from dual citizens convicted of crimes that seriously harm Sweden's "vital interests", saying that it is needed to combat gang criminality.

item.title: Swedish word of the day: mareld
item.description: Today's word of the day is a beautiful natural phenomenon known as 'milky seas' in English.

item.title: Today in Sweden: A roundup of the latest news on Friday
item.description: Government submits bill to double punishments for gang crimes, Sweden to set up centre for Ukrainian refugees, and other news from Sweden on Friday.

item.title: Three Swedish words where the vowel makes all the difference
item.description: There are a lot of vowels in Swedish and it can be easy for someone new to the language to mix them up. Unfortunately, sometimes that means you can accidentally say something obscene when trying to talk about vacuum cleaners.

item.title: 'If I don't have a permit to live in Sweden no one will be willing to invest'
item.description: The former Northvolt worker Abhijith Nag Balasubramanyas launched his own hydroponic microgreens company in Skellefteå in May. But just as he is about to go into commercial production, a warning from the Swedish Migration Agency has put it all under threat.

item.title: My Swedish Career: 'I started a networking group I wish had existed when I came here’
item.description: Elizabeth Wright Veintimilla moved to Sweden almost five years ago after her now-husband was offered a job. After constantly putting herself out there to land a job in the non-profit sector, she had an idea: why not introduce the people she’d been networking with to each other?

item.title: Swedish word of the day: strunta
item.description: Today's Swedish word is one that comes in handy when you just can't be bothered any more.

item.title: EXPLAINED: How to survive Sweden's bizarre home tour ritual
item.description: When visiting a new friend in Sweden, be prepared to be given a bewilderingly thorough tour of every room in the house – sometimes even down to the walk-in wardrobe. This is the 'husesyn' ritual.

item.title: INTERVIEW: ‘Sweden stands fully behind Denmark and Greenland’
item.description: Sweden views US claims to Greenland as ‘very problematic’, but Nato’s newest member still sees the United States as a vital partner for European defence and security, Sweden’s Minister for EU Affairs Jessica Rosencrantz tells The Local.
